newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil over post Gulf War high $235 at close.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil over post Gulf War high $235 at close.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures broke $235 a tonne for the first time since Gulf War hostilities in February 1991 as buyers rushed back in to the market just ahead of the close of trade on Tuesday.
Dealers said gas oil hit the new highs in a rebound from an earlier test of technical support in a market driven by a mixture of speculation and sound supply-demand fundamentals.
"We made a good test of support earlier but fundamental demand just keeps filtering through," said one IPE broker.
Nervous buyers also pitched in ahead of Tuesday's latest weekly American Petroleum Institute inventory statistics, due out after futures markets close.
"The APIs are out tonight and there's some second guessing ahead of that," said the broker.
Gas oil this week had probed its August 1991 high of $235 set during the coup attempt in Russia which failed to unseat President Mikhail Gorbachev.
Low inventories on both sides of the Atlantic have kept buyers on their toes amid fears that an early cold snap could severely stretch supply chains.
November Brent crude futures wiped out earlier losses to reach $23.20 a barrel on Tuesday, back from a low of $22.67 but failed to keep pace with gas oil.
Gas oil's late burst added another 15 cents to its crack spread premium over crude to reach $6.90 a barrel for November contracts at the 1630 GMT close.
